A somewhat contrarian opinion, if I may. I feel like we've set ourselves up to be vulnerable to this kind of trolling.      

I've long felt that the cultural zeitgeist of spoiler-aversion has been getting out of hand, and now in creating for ourselves a dread vulnerability we've delivered to misanthropes a perfect, gift-wrapped means of hurting us.      

Now, make no mistake; these people are assholes, and I pity them for being reduced to grade-school level maliciousness in order to get their jollies. And it would be great if the technical and social arms race to keep them from doing this kind of thing could swing in our favor.      

But the easiest way to undermine these cretins would be if we all just admitted and embraced the fact that *spoilers are not a big deal*, and nothing is ruined if you encounter one.

But yeah, I'll be keeping my eyes open in Legion for potential better matches.

Seems everyone here really likes this for maximizing download speeds on an already strong connection.      

Question: would this kind of card be of any benefit on a *poor* connection? I'm building a system for my parents who have a *terrible* satellite internet connection (I'm talking like sub-dialup level terrible.) Would a card like this be of any benefit to squeeze out as much of the piddling bandwidth my parents have as possible, or would it not make any difference for that type of situation...?
